source.title: Large-Scale Differentially Private BERT
source.authors: Rohan Anil; Badih Ghazi; Vineet Gupta; Ravi Kumar; Pasin Manurangsi

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Reports how batch size and an increasing batch schedule affect held-out MLM accuracy for differentially private BERT-Large, a new setting for the batch-size claim.
record.gate_note: The study reports held-out MLM accuracy and gradient-SNR across batch settings. It does not measure training error or the training-test gap, and it says testing the DP-trained model's generalization ability is future work. Batch-size results use a fixed step budget, not the fixed epoch budget in V5.
record.test_reason: The batch-size experiments fix 20,000 optimizer steps, so larger batches process more examples. They do not test V5's fixed-epoch comparison or its remedies under that comparison. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: mega-batches improve DP BERT-Large utility, and an increasing batch schedule matches fixed-batch accuracy with 14% fewer examples processed. Memorization and further generalization evaluation remain future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses DP-SGD with Adam and weight decay for BERT-Large MLM pretraining; batch-size comparisons use a fixed step budget, and hyperparameters were transferred from non-private tuning at batch size 32K.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes gradient-SNR and MLM accuracy; the increasing batch-size schedule changes training efficiency while matching fixed-batch accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger batches improve DP BERT-Large MLM accuracy at fixed steps and privacy parameters, reaching 60.5% at batch size 2,097,152.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For DP BERT-Large pretraining under this fixed-step recipe, increasing batch size improves MLM accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing batch size from 262,144 to 1,048,576 matches fixed-batch accuracy while processing 14% fewer examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An increasing batch schedule can improve example efficiency in this DP BERT-Large training setting.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: No training error or train-test gap is reported; the paper explicitly leaves testing the DP-trained model's generalization ability for future work. Batch sizes are compared at a fixed step budget, with hyperparameters transferred from tuning at 32K; the text notes that fixed-epoch study would require retuning. Several accuracy values are shown only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: Gradient-SNR measurements in Figures 3a and 4a were left out because they measure gradient-to-noise ratio, not a training-test gap or a measure named in the claim versions. Figure 4b's schedule accuracy comparison is recorded as R5; the figure-only exact values are not recoverable from the text.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization using the same architecture and recipe.
Width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under comparable tuning.
Batch-size effects with epochs held fixed, including whether adapted recipes remove a penalty under that comparison.
Dropout effects and its interaction with training-set size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The decisive mismatch with V5 is the training budget. A training-test gap is not required to test V5, which concerns held-out performance. The supplied text describes accuracy evaluation over 10,000 examples but does not explicitly identify their split.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out performance on natural labels under standard training.
Width sweeps past the interpolation threshold and resulting test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures on image classification.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers and their held-out performance under the described tuning conditions.
The version specifies fixed epoch budgets and workload-dependent batch sizes; this study varies batch size under a fixed step budget in differentially private BERT pretraining.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the training-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting held-out accuracy.
